macro_blurb: Today's tape is shaped by a softer-than-expected US June CPI print at 3.5% annually, with easing energy prices doing much of the work — a disinflation signal relevant for both US and European rate-sensitive sectors. Cutting the other way, US strikes on Iran ahead of a potential Strait of Hormuz blockade reintroduce a Middle East risk premium, particularly for European energy importers and shipping-exposed names. In tech, cybersecurity shares are rallying after IBM's Krishna flagged a shift in AI spending priorities, while a lawsuit from current and former Meta staff alleging AI was used to drive layoff decisions adds a governance overhang to the AI complex. On the EU side, the newly control-free Spain–Gibraltar border removes a lingering post-Brexit friction point.
synthesis:
Today's screen is a US deep-value, high-yield sweep with a rate-sensitive bias. All 10 picks are US-listed — zero European names surfaced — and the composition tilts hard: average Value percentile is 88.1, Yield 83.6, Momentum 83.2, with Quality lagging at 58.9. Seven of ten pay dividend yields above 4%, and three (HPQ, EIX, KHC) sit at or above the 95th percentile on Yield within their sectors. No single sector dominates, but rate-sensitive and cash-return franchises — Utilities (2), Consumer Defensive (2), Financial Services (2) — account for six of the ten. The screen is cheap by construction; it is not high-quality.

The clearest thread runs through the rate-sensitive yield trade: ES and EIX both clear the 90th percentile on Value, Momentum, and Yield within Utilities, and the softer US June CPI print at 3.5% is exactly the backdrop that re-rates regulated names carrying debt/equity of 182 and 226 respectively. A second thread is "cheap but broken": KHC (ROE -12.6%), CNC (ROE -26%), and HPQ (15.3% FCF yield against a PC slump) all screen top-decile on Value with real operational scars behind the multiple. ALL and CINF are the cleaner pair — Value plus Quality both above the 80th percentile, without the impairment tell.

The outlier is BBY: Consumer Cyclical, 100th-percentile Momentum on a +32% three-month run, at a moment when nothing else cyclical made the list. The conspicuous absence is Energy — zero picks despite the Iran strikes and Hormuz risk premium — alongside Real Estate, Basic Materials, and Communication Services. Two macro pivots to watch: a hotter next US CPI would unwind the Utilities re-rating driving ES and EIX, and any Hormuz escalation reprices the energy backdrop this screen is entirely unexposed to.
